newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts post biggest one day gain in five years.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts post biggest one day gain in five years.

text.p: 1522 GMT - UK gilts rocketed by 2-9/32 after UK's Brown raised interest rates by 1/4 pct to 6.25 pct and announced operational independence for BOE. But traders warned of profit taking and saw limited upside potential. * June gilts settle at 113-13/32, up 2-9/32. * June short stg at 93.41, up 0.06

"The effect of this is that the yield curve has flattened quite dramatically. The five-to-10 year (gilt spread) has gone from 25 basis points to 16 basis points and the 10-year to ultra-longs has gone from 15 to 12 basis points," the trader said.
But there was little prospect of short-term gains, traders said, as profit-takers stood ready to move in and capitalise on the rally made during a hectic session.

"You couldn't deal in size for about an hour this morning. Market-makers were not prepared to make quotes in a decent size. Many of the systems couldn't cope with a two point rise," one trader said of the manic market.
Over 220,000 lots of the June future changed hands in pit trading. And the prospect of further interest rate hikes to stem inflationary pressures also dented gilt's short-term attraction.
"I think given the government's target of keeping inflation at 2.5 percent, and the momentum in the economy they will need more than one 1/4 percent rise," another trader said.
"It will certainly need some fairly severe tax measures and I think with those tax measures will come with another rate rise."

Traders said Brown's decision to give the Bank of England greater operational independence not only offered the prospect of lower inflation but was also a step towards Britain participating in European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
They did point out, however, that though central bank independence is a necessary requirement for participation in EMU, the Labour government is committed to a referendum on EMU.
Gilts massively outperformed other bond markets and the yield spread to Bunds narrowed dramatically, to 147 basis points from 173 at the open.
